identifying and validating novel targets for the treatment of cardiovascular disease, particularly heart failure, using molecular and cell biology approaches.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

PKGIα is an antiremodeling kinase in the heart that phosphorylates cMyBP-C at the M-domain and that this phosphorylation is a potential therapeutic target to circumvent the vasodilatory side effects associated with PKG activators.
PKGI phosphorylates cMyBP-C in vitro, and in cells and animals in vivo, and that PKGI phosphorylation of cMyBP-C may be a novel mechanism of PKGI-mediated cardiac protection against remodeling.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PKGI is a kinase that is activated by cGMP.
cGMP-dependent Protein Kinase I (PKG) is a kinase that can regulate a variety of proteins, but the specific proteins are unknown and we are trying to identify them.

we identified a new protein kinase G-I&agr;-dependent substrate in cardiac myosin-binding protein-C, and we demonstrated that this protein kinase G-Iα substrate can regulate cardiac remodeling in a manner that may be beneficial to the heart.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a novel substrate for protein kinase G (PKG) in the heart.
PKGIα is an important kinase for cardiac myocyte survival.
cMyBP is a substrate for PKG in the heart.
